newsitem.title: CHINA: HK gold ends sharply lower on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends sharply lower on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended sharply lower on Wednesday from New York's previous close, dropping more than US$4 an ounce as U.S. fund selling and sell orders from London poured into Asian markets, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$315.40/90 an ounce compared to New York's close at US$319.80/320.30 on Tuesday.
Sources said U.S. fund selling had continued well into Asian trading hours and that when London opened, hefty sell orders pushed the market down steeply in early afternoon trade.
"Everyone is selling today," said one source.
Dealers also reported Australian producer selling, but said it had been overshadowed by fund selling.
"Lease rates have gone up, funds need to borrow gold to finance short positions," another dealer said.
Physical demand has been steady but slowed after gold bounced back to $318 from lows near $314.
Swinging prices made physical buyers wary and they were waiting to see whether gold would sink lower before buying actively, dealers said.
Local tael gold ended HK$25 lower at HK$2,928 per tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +1.00 from its previous fix at nil.
